facts.title: Experience League: What is Target?
facts.quote: Adobe Target, part of the Adobe Experience Cloud, offers comprehensive tools to personalize customer experiences across web, mobile sites, apps, social media, and other digital channels.
facts.supports: Adobe describes Target as its tool for personalizing customer experiences on the web and other digital channels.

facts.title: Experience League: Which Activity Types Are Available in Target?
facts.quote: Compares two or more experiences to see which experience best improves conversions throughout a pre-specified test period.
facts.supports: Adobe's description of a manual A/B Test activity in Target.

facts.title: Experience League: What Is an Experience Targeting (XT) Activity?
facts.quote: Experience Targeting (XT) delivers content to a specific audience based on a set of marketer-defined rules and criteria.
facts.supports: Experience Targeting shows chosen content to a chosen audience by rule, which is how a known-customer audience gets its own experience.

facts.title: Experience League: What is an Automated Personalization (AP) Activity?
facts.quote: Automated Personalization (AP) activities in Adobe Target combine offers or messages, and uses advanced machine learning to match different offer variations to each visitor based on their individual customer profile to personalize content and drive lift.
facts.supports: Adobe's description of Automated Personalization in Target.

facts.title: Experience League: What is Target Recommendations?
facts.quote: Adobe Target Recommendations activities automatically display products, services, or content that might interest your visitors based on previous user activity, preferences, or other criteria.
facts.supports: Adobe's description of Recommendations activities in Target.

facts.title: Experience League: How Do I Implement with the Experience Platform Web SDK?
facts.quote: Adobe Experience Platform Web SDK (AEP Web SDK) is a client-side JavaScript library that allows customers of Adobe Experience Cloud to interact with the various services in the Adobe Experience Cloud (including Target) through the Adobe Experience Platform Edge Network.
facts.supports: Target can be implemented on the site through the Experience Platform Web SDK and the Edge Network.

facts.title: Experience League: Real-Time Customer Data Platform Overview
facts.quote: Built on Adobe Experience Platform, Adobe Real-Time Customer Data Platform (Real-Time CDP) helps companies bring together known and anonymous data from multiple enterprise sources in order to create customer profiles that can be used to provide personalized customer experiences across all channels and devices in real time.
facts.supports: Real-Time CDP brings known and anonymous data together into customer profiles used for personalization.

facts.title: Experience League: Real-Time Customer Data Platform Overview
facts.quote: Real-Time CDP includes tools for data governance, identity management, advanced segmentation, and data science so that you can build profiles and define audiences, as well as derive rich insights while being able to enforce strict data governance policies.
facts.supports: Real-Time CDP includes identity management, segmentation and data governance for building profiles and defining audiences.

facts.title: Experience League: Real-Time Customer Data Platform Overview
facts.quote: Real-Time CDP connects to a large ecosystem of partners, not to mention native integrations with Adobe CX Enterprise, so you can seamlessly activate these audiences and deliver great customer experiences across all channels, from on-site or in-app personalization to email, paid media, call centers, connected devices, and more.
facts.supports: Real-Time CDP activates audiences to Adobe applications and partners, including for on-site personalization.

facts.title: Experience League: Segmentation Service Overview
facts.quote: Adobe Experience Platform Segmentation Service provides a user interface and RESTful API that allows you to create audiences through segment definitions or other sources from your Real-Time Customer Profile data.
facts.supports: Audiences are built from Real-Time Customer Profile data with the Segmentation Service.

facts.title: Experience League: How Do I Integrate Target with the Real-Time Customer Data Platform?
facts.quote: The Adobe Target destination in Real-Time CDP allows you to use Experience Platform segments in Adobe Target for same page-personalization and next-page personalization with governance and privacy support.
facts.supports: The Adobe Target destination makes Experience Platform audiences usable in Target for same-page and next-page personalization.

facts.title: Experience League: Frequently asked questions
facts.quote: Attributes will be available to use in Target in JSON and HTML offers.
facts.supports: Profile attributes activated to the Adobe Target destination can be used in Target's JSON and HTML offers.

facts.title: Experience League: Adobe Target connection
facts.quote: To achieve same-page and next-page personalization use cases, you must use a datastream when configuring the Adobe Target connection.
facts.supports: Same-page and next-page personalization require the Adobe Target connection to be set up with a datastream.

facts.title: Experience League: Activate audiences to edge personalization destinations
facts.quote: Adobe Experience Platform uses edge segmentation together with edge destinations to enable customers to create and target audiences at high scale, in real time.
facts.supports: Edge segmentation with edge destinations (such as Adobe Target) is what enables real-time audience targeting.

facts.title: Experience League: Activate audiences to edge personalization destinations
facts.quote: The Active-On-Edge merge policy ensures that audiences are constantly evaluated on the edge and are available for real-time and next-page personalization use case.
facts.supports: Audiences sent to edge destinations need an Active-On-Edge merge policy.

facts.title: Experience League: Using identityMap in Data Collection
facts.quote: When a visitor signs in, completes a purchase, or otherwise becomes known, you can send person-level identifiers (CRM ID, hashed email, loyalty ID, etc.) alongside the ECID.
facts.supports: When a visitor signs in, the site sends a person-level identifier such as a CRM ID alongside the device-level ECID.

facts.title: Experience League: Identity Service Overview
facts.quote: You log in with your username and password combination to an e-commerce website using your laptop. This event qualifies you as an authenticated user, thus Identity Service recognizes your CRMID.
facts.supports: Identity Service recognises an authenticated (signed-in) user by a person identifier such as a CRM ID.

facts.title: Experience League: Merge Policies Overview
facts.quote: Identity stitching (ID stitching) is the process of identifying data fragments and combining them together to form a complete profile record.
facts.supports: Adobe's definition of identity stitching in Real-Time Customer Profile merge policies.

facts.title: Experience League: Merge Policies Overview
facts.quote: When bringing this data together, merge policies are the rules that Experience Platform uses to determine how data will be prioritized and what data will be combined to create a unified view.
facts.supports: Merge policies decide how data from several sources is combined into one customer profile.

facts.title: Experience League: Adobe Target connection
facts.quote: First-login personalization requires the primary identity in the personalization request to match the known customer identity in the Real-Time CDP identity graph.
facts.supports: For the Adobe Target connection, personalizing at first login depends on the request's primary identity matching the known customer identity.

facts.title: Experience League: Customer Journey Analytics overview
facts.quote: Customer Journey Analytics is Adobe’s next-generation Analytics solution that lets you use the power of Analysis Workspace with data from Adobe Experience Platform.
facts.supports: Customer Journey Analytics is Adobe's analytics product that works on Experience Platform data in Analysis Workspace.

facts.title: Experience League: Customer Journey Analytics overview
facts.quote: You can view and analyze data sequentially, spanning multiple channels. Data from your call center, POS systems, and online properties can be combined into a single reporting view.
facts.supports: Customer Journey Analytics analyzes data across channels in a single reporting view.

facts.title: Experience League: Experimentation panel
facts.quote: The Experimentation panel lets analysts compare different user experiences, marketing, or messaging variations to determine which is best at driving a specific outcome.
facts.supports: The Experimentation panel compares variants to find which best drives an outcome.

facts.title: Experience League: Experimentation panel
facts.quote: You can evaluate the lift and confidence of any A/B experiment from any experimentation platform: online, offline, from Adobe solutions like Target or Journey Optimizer, and even BYO (bring-your-own) data.
facts.supports: The Experimentation panel reports lift and confidence for A/B experiments, including ones from Adobe Target.

facts.title: Experience League: Experimentation panel
facts.quote: The Experiment report summary shows the Lift over Baseline, which is a measure of the percentage improvement in the conversion rate of a given variant over the baseline.
facts.supports: How Adobe defines lift in the Experimentation panel.

facts.title: Experience League: What is Target reporting in Adobe Customer Journey Analytics?
facts.quote: To use Customer Journey Analytics as the reporting source for Target, both you and your company must have access to Customer Journey Analytics and to Target.
facts.supports: Using Customer Journey Analytics as Target's reporting source requires access to both products.

facts.title: Experience League: What is Target reporting in Adobe Customer Journey Analytics?
facts.quote: This integration is not the same as Adobe Analytics for Target (A4T). The implementation and supported activity types are different.
facts.supports: Adobe states the Target and Customer Journey Analytics integration is not A4T.

facts.title: Experience League: What is Target reporting in Adobe Customer Journey Analytics?
facts.quote: Auto-Target and Automated Personalization activities do not yet support Customer Journey Analytics as the reporting source.
facts.supports: Auto-Target and Automated Personalization activities cannot report in Customer Journey Analytics through this integration.

facts.title: Experience League: setConsent (Web SDK)
facts.quote: The setConsent command tells the Web SDK if it should send data (opt in), discard data (opt out), or use defaultConsent (consent unknown).
facts.supports: The Web SDK's setConsent command controls whether data is sent or discarded according to the visitor's consent.

facts.title: Experience League: Automatic Policy Enforcement
facts.quote: To help safeguard your organization from potential risks and liabilities, Experience Platform automatically enforces usage policies should any violations occur when activating audiences to destinations.
facts.supports: Experience Platform enforces data usage policies automatically when audiences are activated to destinations.

facts.title: Experience League: Frequently asked questions
facts.quote: The Data Governance and Consent Policies created and associated with the selected marketing actions will govern the activation of the selected attributes.
facts.supports: Adobe's FAQ for the Adobe Target and Custom Personalization destinations says governance and consent policies govern what is activated.

facts.title: Experience League: Automatic Policy Enforcement
facts.quote: Consent policies are only available for organizations that have purchased Adobe Healthcare Shield or Adobe Privacy & Security Shield.
facts.supports: Consent policies need the Healthcare Shield or Privacy & Security Shield add-on.

facts.title: Experience League: Adobe Target connection
facts.quote: The Adobe Target destination is now available to organizations with Adobe Journey Optimizer, in addition to organizations with Real-Time CDP.
facts.supports: The Adobe Target destination card requires a Real-Time CDP or Journey Optimizer entitlement (changelog entry dated August 2026).

facts.title: Experience League: Adobe Target connection
facts.quote: Having access to this destination card does not mean that Adobe Target itself is provisioned for your organization. To complete setup, you also need Adobe Target and a Target-enabled datastream, meaning a datastream with the Adobe Target service enabled.
facts.supports: Adobe Target must be licensed and provisioned separately, with a datastream that has the Adobe Target service enabled.

facts.title: Experience League: What is an Automated Personalization (AP) Activity?
facts.quote: Automated Personalization is available as part of the Target Premium solution. This feature is not available in Target Standard without a Target Premium license.
facts.supports: Automated Personalization requires a Target Premium license.

not_found: claim 8: no Adobe page states a required Adobe Target edition (Standard or Premium) for receiving Real-Time CDP audiences. The Adobe Target connection page (experience-platform/destinations/catalog/personalization/adobe-target-connection) only lists the Real-Time CDP or Journey Optimizer entitlement, says Adobe Target must be provisioned, and links to permission guides for both Target Premium and Target Standard.

claim 8: no quotable sentence on which Real-Time CDP tier is needed. The Target guide page (target/using/integrate/integrating-with-rtcdp) says 'RTCDP (any SKU) and Target' for Web SDK implementations and 'RTCDP (Premium or Ultimate) and Target' for at.js, but only as table cells, so they are not quoted.

claim 7: no Experience League page describes Privacy and Security Shield or Healthcare Shield as products. Tried experience-platform/landing/governance-privacy-security/privacy-and-security-shield and /healthcare-shield (both 404); Adobe's docs link the names to business.adobe.com, which is blocked here. Only the mentions quoted in the facts and cautions were found.

claim 6: no Adobe page uses the name 'A4T for CJA'. The Customer Journey Analytics guide has no Target integration page of its own (analytics-platform/using/integrations/a4t and analytics-platform/using/cja-usecases/experimentation/target are 404); its Experimentation panel page links to the Target guide page target/using/integrate/cja/target-reporting-in-cja.
claim 4: nothing specific to banks or financial services on the identity, profile or merge policy pages; the examples are e-commerce logins.
cautions: Do not call the measurement integration A4T: 'This integration is not the same as Adobe Analytics for Target (A4T).' https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/target/using/integrate/cja/target-reporting-in-cja

Customer Journey Analytics reporting for Target does not yet support Auto-Target or Automated Personalization activities; choosing a data view and a Customer Journey Analytics metric in Target is offered only for A/B activities with manual traffic split or Auto-Allocate (not Experience Targeting, Multivariate Test or Recommendations). Same URL.

The Target and Customer Journey Analytics integration has no pre-built report ('Activity reports must be built in Customer Journey Analytics'), the reporting source cannot be changed after an activity goes live, and an activity can use only one reporting source. Persistence must be configured on the Activity dimensions or only same-event metrics are linked. Same URL.

The Experimentation panel needs the Experimentation Experiment and Experimentation Variant context labels set in the data view, and 'currently does not support analysis of A/A tests'. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/analytics-platform/using/cja-workspace/panels/experimentation

Automated Personalization and Recommendations activities are Target Premium only. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/target/using/activities/automated-personalization/automated-personalization and https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/target/using/recommendations/recommendations

Same-page and next-page personalization need the Web SDK or Edge Network API plus a datastream; 'if at.js is used instead of Web SDK, only next-session personalization is supported.' https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/destinations/destinations-faq

Audiences activated to Adobe Target must use an active-on-edge merge policy (the FAQ says there can be only one), audience definitions take up to one hour to reach the Edge Network, at most 30 attributes per sandbox can be activated, and only static single-value attributes are supported. Same FAQ URL.

Known customers at first login: 'If the primary identity is an ECID or an unstitched identity, identity reconciliation may take several minutes before edge personalization reflects the known customer's data.' Edge profiles also expire after 14 days of inactivity. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/destinations/catalog/personalization/adobe-target-connection
With a custom Target workspace, mapped attributes still go to the default Target workspace ('This behavior will change in a future update'). Same Adobe Target connection URL.

Data residency for a bank: 'The edge data will be stored in an edge server location closest to where it was collected. This data may also be stored in a location other than the one designated as the hub (or principal) Adobe Experience Platform data center.' https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/segmentation/methods/edge-segmentation

Consent: the Web SDK automatically enforces only the data collection permission; 'While more granular consents and preferences can be collected and persisted in customer profiles, these additional signals must be manually enforced in your own downstream processes.'. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/landing/governance-privacy-security/consent/adobe/overview

Adobe's pages disagree on consent policies. The automatic enforcement page says consent policies need Healthcare Shield or Privacy & Security Shield (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/data-governance/enforcement/auto-enforcement), while the destinations FAQ says the Adobe Target destination is integrated with Data Usage Labels and the Consent Policy Enforcement Service and 'These features are available for all customers', and also that consent policy management at scale requires Privacy & Security Shield. Confirm with Adobe before promising consent policy enforcement.

Data usage policies are disabled by default and enforce nothing until enabled; the destination-level consent exclusion on the automatic enforcement page is marked '(Beta)'. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/data-governance/policies/overview

Sensitive data add-ons: the destinations FAQ says 'Adobe Target is not HIPPA-compliant with Adobe Healthcare Shield' (Adobe's spelling). That is about health data, not banking, but it shows the Shield add-ons do not extend to Target.

Naming: the Real-Time CDP overview (updated November 6, 2026) says 'Adobe CX Enterprise' where Target's pages still say 'Adobe Experience Cloud'. Quotes are verbatim, so the two names will appear side by side.

The Target guide's implementation table lists 'RTCDP (Premium or Ultimate)' for at.js, while the Real-Time CDP overview names the tiers Prime and Ultimate. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/target/using/integrate/integrating-with-rtcdp
